motion.purpose: Button active-state press scale (scale-x-97 scale-y-98) with a 150ms delay.

motion.name: post-preview-transition
motion.purpose: Shared-element morph transition between blog post previews and their destination posts, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: link-hover-underline-lift
motion.value: 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94); text-underline-offset 2px → 4px alongside the link/link-hover color shift
motion.purpose: The site-wide link hover cue: the underline pulls away from the text while the color shifts red→orange, so hover reads even for readers who don't perceive the color change. Runs faster than the general 300ms color-transition token because it's on the highest-frequency interactive element on the page.

narrative.northStar: Technical editorial with a restrained personality
narrative.overview:
The site serves as a developer's digital garden - half personal blog, half living web-development reference - aimed at an audience that appreciates density, precision, and the occasional bit of wit. It is built from Koh Samui, Thailand, and the design echoes that contradiction: deeply technical but unhurried.

The visual language is built around three constraints: a warm, near-neutral gray palette as the base (not cool, not clinical); a single accent pair (a burnt-orange primary shifting to a darker tone on hover) that signals every interactive element without overwhelming the content; and variable-weight typography that can express both the weight of a technical headline and the lightness of body prose without switching families.

The overriding aesthetic is engineered lightness: generous line heights, minimal corner radii, no decorative shadows - hierarchy is achieved through tone, scale, and spacing rather than visual ornament.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, near-neutral gray palette as the structural base
Single accent hue (burnt orange) reserved for interactive elements
Variable-weight typography spanning display headlines to body prose
Engineered lightness: minimal radii, tonal depth instead of shadows

rules.name: The Unlayered Hover Rule
rules.body: Link hover color rules must live in @layer utilities, not @layer base: .typography-reading's inlined prose styles (@layer components) set a fixed, non-hover color on every link inside article text, and @layer components always outranks @layer base regardless of selector specificity. Also, @apply hover:*/dark:*/dark:hover:* chains silently fail to compile when applied onto a bare tag selector (confirmed on Tailwind 4.3.3, no build error) - write the variant as literal CSS instead.

dos: Do use font-changa only for headings and display text - never for body copy or code.
Do apply the primary color exclusively to interactive primary actions (CTAs, hover states). One per screen is ideal.
Do maintain WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for normal text). The on-surface / on-surface-dark tokens are calibrated for this.
Do use transition-colors duration-300 ease-in-out for all color-based hover transitions to maintain consistent motion rhythm.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion - the LetterGlitch canvas animation, view transitions, and all keyframe animations must be gated behind the no-preference media query.
Do prefix any temporary debugging class with debug (for example debug-outline) if one is ever needed, so it can't be mistaken for an intentional style and is easy to grep for before committing.

Do derive tinted/frosted surfaces (header, popovers, breadcrumb pills) from var(--background) via color-mix() or a black/white opacity overlay - never pick an independent gray/olive shade for a "raised" or "frosted" look.

Do use the shadcn primitives (Input/Textarea in src/components/forms/, Button/Card in src/components/shared/elements/) as the canonical class recipe for form-like elements, even when the actual markup is a native, vanilla-JS-driven element rather than a hydrated React island.
donts: Don't add box-shadows in dark mode - use outline outline-white/10 to define surfaces instead.

Don't apply the contrast rule to elements marked data-dnb-design-exception="decorative-low-contrast" - they are hidden from assistive technology and intentionally fail contrast as decorative background texture.
Don't use rounded-xl on outer containers - it belongs only to images inside cards.
Don't introduce font weights above 400 for Changa One - no bold weight exists in the loaded font file.
Don't add decorative gradient backgrounds or overlapping color layers to page sections - depth comes from tonal step-ups, not color mixing.
Don't give the same tinted surface a different opacity per theme (for example 70% light / 92% dark) - share one value via a custom property so light and dark can't drift apart.
Don't extend the olive surface scale into structural neutrals - text, borders, and muted-foreground stay on gray. olive is reserved for --background and things derived from it.
Don't rely on @tailwindcss/forms' class-strategy names like form-input - this project runs the plugin in base strategy, so that class doesn't exist and silently does nothing.
Don't introduce off-brand accent hues (indigo, blue, etc.) left over from a copied template - map every interactive/active/focus state to the orange primary or red link pair.
